mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS below 2.0%) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the cost of capital decreases for corporate cash flows.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 2.0% is followed by negative 20d SPX returns in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months but SPX 5d returns are positive in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% in the prior month indicate a broad-based demand contraction, reducing corporate revenue expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST decline > 0.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: RSAFS and HOUST decline > 0.5% in the prior month but SPX 60d returns are positive in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production (INDPRO above 105.0) indicates easing supply chain bottlenecks, reducing inflationary pressures and lowering the probability of aggressive monetary tightening, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 105.0 but SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 3.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening, increasing the cost of capital and slowing economic growth, which causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 3.0% but SPX 5d returns are positive in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.0% year-over-year indicates persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy and increasing real interest rates, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in the prior month but SPX 60d returns are positive in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 signals a manufacturing slowdown, reducing corporate output and profits, which causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100.0 but SPX 20d returns are positive in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts (HOUST) decline below 1400.0 (thousands) signals weakening residential construction, a key driver of consumer spending, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST < 1400.0 but SPX 5d returns are positive in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.
